terra.problem: He comments on his own teaching with “Sometimes the best teaching is just reading what's on the page.”
Telling the baker to multiply the biggest gust they've experienced assigns the wind a magnitude the text doesn't give.
The text doesn't say the sailors cried out at once or that they were on a wet deck.
“Nearly breaking apart” goes beyond the text, which says the ship was in danger of breaking apart.
The captain's words are given, but the text doesn't describe his manner as ungentle or say Jonah was in a bunk.
“Nobody raises a hand” asserts a detail the text doesn't give.
The text says the captain approached and spoke to Jonah, but doesn't say he woke him.
The text doesn't say Jonah was standing or that the ship was in the middle of the sea.
He calls the claim about God ruling from the temple in Jerusalem a true Bible fact without a reference supporting it.
The text says Jonah had told the men he was fleeing, but doesn't say they had just learned it.
The men tried to row back to land; the text doesn't say they tried everything else first.
The movie comparison repeats the joke idea from stop 1, card 3, answer 3.
The text says the raging sea grew calm, not that the storm stopped.
“Started the day” adds a time the text doesn't give.
For “thank,” the explanation points to “vows,” although “fear” is the word that fits that blank.
